title: AI and the EU Digital Markets Act: Addressing the Risks of Bigness in Generative AI
venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 202, 2023
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the regulatory risks posed by the rapid growth and concentration of generative AI markets. The authors argue that existing competition and platform regulations in the European Union, especially the Digital Markets Act (DMA), do not adequately cover generative AI systems that may become dominant gateways for AI-based services.

Rather than presenting an empirical study or educational intervention, the paper develops a policy and legal framework for classifying certain generative AI services as "core platform services" and certain providers as "gatekeepers" under the DMA. It discusses how generative AI can be delivered as a platform through products like ChatGPT-style services and APIs, and it identifies sources of gatekeeping power such as compute resources, early-mover advantages, data accumulation, and integration with other services.

The paper is set in the European Union regulatory context and focuses on market structure and governance, not on a human participant population. Its main conclusion is that the DMA should be amended or interpreted to explicitly include generative AI services in order to preserve contestability, fairness, diversity, and innovation, and to prevent a few large firms from becoming entrenched gatekeepers in the generative AI ecosystem.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI systems such as large language model chatbots and related foundation-model services used for text, image, and other content generation.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is a theoretical/policy analysis of generative AI as a market and platform layer under the EU Digital Markets Act, not an empirical evaluation in education.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual and policy analysis paper, not an empirical study of an AI tool in K-12 education. It does not present a study design, sample, or outcome evaluation.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational outcomes, effect sizes, or measured impacts are reported. The paper discusses regulatory risks and market structure rather than instructional effectiveness or harm in classrooms.
